methods.label: Typographic order and negative space
methods.purpose: Give heterogeneous content a coherent reading order through proportion, alignment and negative space.
translate: Choose a dominant type/image relationship and a few shared baselines; the grid can remain invisible.
Let headings, captions and prose occupy their own natural measures; use unused columns as counterspace, not filler.
methods.implementation: Derive tracks and spacing from actual content. Test long titles and captions; choose new local anchors when narrow screens change the relationship.
methods.motion: A geometric reveal may follow an existing edge or baseline; motion is optional and the resting composition carries the identity.
methods.narrow: Regroup the reading order rather than shrinking a poster or preserving every column.
methods.fallback: A complete static composition with the same hierarchy and meaningful empty space.
watchFor: Visible grid lines mistaken for hierarchy
Equal occupancy and repeated full-width bands
renderQuestions: Does the thumbnail have a dominant relationship?
Do actual prose and images retain different measures at intermediate widths?

methods.label: Editorial selection and reading rhythm
methods.purpose: Make content feel edited through selection, pacing and type/image relationships.
translate: Separate the display voice, reading voice and metadata; a paper tint alone supplies no editorial point of view.
Alternate concentrated evidence with a useful pause according to content; choose what each medium expresses best.
methods.implementation: Build with finished headlines, real images, captions and body passages. Own the type system instead of copying proprietary fonts or measured values.
methods.motion: Reveal a relevant caption or reading state without moving the passage the visitor is currently reading.
methods.narrow: Preserve content priority and legible passages; recompose the image/title relationship independently.
methods.fallback: Normal document flow with complete text, media credits and destinations.
watchFor: A beige skin used as a substitute for editing
Decorative headings with interchangeable content
renderQuestions: Can the reader tell what matters before reading every paragraph?
Does the full page vary its reading distance without filler sections?

methods.label: Typography as a moving image
methods.purpose: Let words carry the subject, emphasis and temporal composition.
translate: Choreograph semantic word groups with contrasting scale, weight, mask and position; each pause should hold as a designed frame.
Choose motion that expresses the phrase rather than applying one entrance effect to every letter.
methods.implementation: Load and measure real fonts before captures. Keep a readable semantic text layer; reserve authored outlines or media for expression that live text cannot reproduce.
methods.motion: Specify readable hold, transition and final state for the target phrase. Use mass or anticipation only when the meaning benefits; no universal easing or duration is inferred from the cases.
methods.narrow: Recompose word groups for actual line lengths; do not scale a wide title sequence into tiny type.
methods.fallback: The final or selected static typographic frame retains the complete message.
watchFor: Animation required to discover the message
Clipped text or endless replay preventing reading
renderQuestions: Is a still frame intentional and readable?
Do the start, transition and settled states preserve the whole phrase?

methods.label: Hanzi structure and motion
methods.purpose: Author Chinese typography from strokes, balance and character structure.
translate: Inspect the selected glyph's horizontal/vertical rhythm, internal space and center of gravity before deciding motion.
Choose whole-character or semantic phrase movement when stroke-level authorship is unavailable; do not simulate calligraphy by spreading Latin-style letter spacing.
methods.implementation: Use actual licensed Chinese glyphs. Stroke reveals need deliberately authored contours or high-quality original media, not guessed stroke paths; keep the full text accessible.
methods.motion: Let reveal direction or transformation follow an evidenced glyph relationship; preserve recognition through the expressive moment.
methods.narrow: Test punctuation, mixed scripts and the longest real phrase; permit a new arrangement with its own optical balance.
methods.fallback: A recognizable complete character or phrase in a balanced static composition.
watchFor: Latin animation transplanted without examining the glyph
Broken recognition or incorrect invented strokes
renderQuestions: Do characters remain recognizable at their actual viewing size?
Does the phrase retain its meaning with animation disabled?

methods.label: Information choreography and focus
methods.purpose: Guide attention through information and state changes without losing context.
translate: Separate the important new fact, supporting context and persistent identity; preserve the subject while information changes.
Translate film editing into user-controlled steps, a meaningful live state or a bounded demonstration; playback cadence does not dictate reading speed.
methods.implementation: Name trigger, old/new information, focus target and settled result. Show actual product behavior or label a simulation; never fake real work with animated UI blocks.
methods.motion: Use stagger, replacement or a focus shift for a named relationship. Replay and interruption must settle cleanly without hiding controls.
methods.narrow: Give the important information normal readable width; borrow broadcast hierarchy without inheriting tiny text in a narrow strip.
methods.fallback: Persistent context and the complete current/final information remain reachable without playback.
watchFor: Automatic cuts while the visitor reads
Focus moving away from the changed result
renderQuestions: Can the user identify what changed?
Does interruption leave a usable, truthful state?

methods.label: Print grain and halftone material
methods.purpose: Use controlled image/material treatment to give content a physical character.
translate: Choose dot size, contrast and grain scale at the intended viewing size; inspect the source before attributing its exact technique.
Let a pattern derive from the subject or identity; keep the featured work distinguishable from its supporting material.
methods.implementation: Create or source high-quality texture/processed imagery. Treat the media layer separately from semantic text; check pattern artifacts at actual device pixel ratios.
methods.motion: A material reveal may expose a specific image or detail; constant texture flicker is not required.
methods.narrow: Retune texture scale and inspect moire, subject recognition and text contrast.
methods.fallback: A clean static subject image or stable printed treatment with all content intact.
watchFor: Noise over small text
Low-quality image hidden behind a filter
renderQuestions: Does the subject remain clear?
Is the material convincing at actual size rather than only in a mockup?

methods.label: Papercraft depth and assembly
methods.purpose: Build subject-specific physical depth through layered material and deliberate assembly.
translate: Observe cut edges, contact shadows, thickness and physical movement as related properties.
Use an original paper object or scene to express the subject; a generic drop shadow is not papercraft.
methods.implementation: Use provided material, real production assets, or deliberately generated original imagery inspected at delivery size. Video/frame sequences need a good poster and loading/failure behavior.
methods.motion: Assembly or replacement can follow physical pieces; use deliberate frame timing only where it supports the material.
methods.narrow: Reframe the actual scene so its important pieces remain inspectable; do not shrink them into decorative thumbnails.
methods.fallback: A high-quality finished-scene still with the same subject and meaning.
watchFor: Artificial texture and implausible lighting
Heavy media with a weak or missing static frame
renderQuestions: Do shadows and edges imply the same material?
Does the original subject remain legible in the fallback?

methods.label: Evidence and data as a narrative
methods.purpose: Turn real evidence, a process or personal data into an understandable sequence.
translate: Choose a concrete question and the evidence that answers it; let each view establish a fact or relationship.
Let illustration explain the actual process and data carry meaning; do not replace facts with attractive metaphors or generic stat cards.
methods.implementation: Use attributable content, honest data, units and comparable scales. Sketch the explanatory sequence before polishing a chart or illustration; label sample data clearly.
methods.motion: Reveal a comparison or process change at a pace the user can inspect; preserve the underlying evidence.
methods.narrow: Reorder the explanation and annotations for the small canvas; retain units, context and access to detail.
methods.fallback: The same findings are available as static graphics and readable text or data.
watchFor: Invented achievements or statistics
Illustration that says nothing about the actual process
renderQuestions: Can the viewer explain the relationship afterward?
Is every visible claim supported by real or explicitly sample evidence?

methods.label: Optical material and continuous fields
methods.purpose: Establish depth or a coherent identity through light, material and continuous movement.
translate: Define foreground, background and an actual material relationship before choosing blur, reflection or a wave.
Keep the subject and information hierarchy visible; a supplied or authored direction can choose an expressive field without making it a universal skin.
methods.implementation: Inspect the relevant official guidance or original asset. Validate contrast against actual background states; use a lightweight compatible implementation with a solid/static substitute.
methods.motion: A continuous field should have a clear identity or spatial purpose; its movement must not obscure controls or reading.
methods.narrow: Check cropping, layer legibility and low-power behavior; simplify the expensive material where necessary.
methods.fallback: A solid material or good static field preserves depth cues and readable content.
watchFor: All regions becoming glass panels
Generic mesh blobs substituted for an inspected source's material
renderQuestions: Is depth still understandable without animation or blur?
Does contrast hold across the changing background?

methods.label: Assertive graphic contrast
methods.purpose: Create a deliberate graphic hierarchy through weight, color, geometry and tension.
translate: Decide which object owns the contrast; let unequal areas, type weight or offset geometry create a specific relationship.
Hard edges may be an authored choice; distinguish that choice from mechanically outlining every section.
methods.implementation: Compose actual content before adding thick borders or offset shadows. Let project/reference authority override advisory soft-shape preferences when supported by the render.
methods.motion: An offset, collision or geometric change may acknowledge a meaningful action; stable control geometry still matters.
methods.narrow: Rebalance contrast and spatial tension for the available area; keep text and actions reachable.
methods.fallback: The static graphic hierarchy retains its emphasis and usable controls.
watchFor: Every region competing at maximum contrast
A border treatment standing in for a composition
renderQuestions: Does one relationship lead?
Is the strong geometry purposeful in the target content?

methods.label: Ornament derived from type and structure
methods.purpose: Give a subject a distinctive ornamental rhythm tied to its structure and typography.
translate: Derive repeated proportions, terminals or motifs from the chosen title or subject.
A coherent ornamental system can use many palettes; black and gold alone do not establish Art Deco.
methods.implementation: Inspect the actual source and create original lettering or artwork when needed; keep operational labels and body passages readable.
methods.motion: A motif can unfold or frame a meaningful title/detail without requiring every passage to animate.
methods.narrow: Retain the important motif relationship with enough space for the actual title; recompose dense ornament.
methods.fallback: A complete static title or motif retains the identity.
watchFor: Stock gold decoration unrelated to the subject
Ornament reducing legibility
renderQuestions: Does the motif belong to this work?
Does its type/ornament relationship survive small sizes?

methods.label: Directional and diagonal tension
methods.purpose: Use directional relationships to express movement or tension in the subject.
translate: Choose a dominant vector and counterweight through crop, type grouping or spatial movement.
Express direction in the authored object while keeping long passages and repeated controls convenient to read.
methods.implementation: Inspect the source, compose the actual phrase/object and test its bounds. Avoid page-wide transforms that accidentally crop content or change control hit areas.
methods.motion: The entry or state change can follow the chosen vector and settle into a readable composition.
methods.narrow: Rechoose direction and line grouping when the original diagonal no longer fits.
methods.fallback: A stable directional still with full content and predictable controls.
watchFor: Rotation mistaken for a point of view
Clipping, overflow or awkward target geometry
renderQuestions: Does the direction express the target subject?
Are all words and controls reachable at narrow widths?

methods.label: Authored light and retro signal
methods.purpose: Give a specific scene or interface a coherent light/signal language.
translate: Choose what emits light, what receives it and which signal belongs to the subject.
Build a consistent scene or original asset rather than stacking unrelated glows, chromatic offsets and scanlines.
methods.implementation: Use high-quality original media or a meaningful rendered scene. Keep texture/distortion separate from operational text and provide explicit playback control where appropriate.
methods.motion: Light or signal changes can follow an actual scene event/state; continuous flicker is not required for the identity.
methods.narrow: Reframe the important object and inspect dark detail, luminous contrast and texture at actual device size.
methods.fallback: A clear still scene or stable signal state with all content intact.
watchFor: Unreadable small text behind CRT effects
Generic neon atmosphere with no inspectable subject
renderQuestions: Are the light sources and material response coherent?
Can the subject and current state be understood without moving effects?
